questions.stem: Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic which draws the fluid from ICF to ECF by osmosis. Which of the following condition is a contraindication for the Mannitol administration?
questions.solutionHtml:
Acute pulmonary edema

Mannitol:

  • Osmotic diuretics like mannitol will be present in the extracellular fluid and increase extracellular osmolality.
  • Thereby water is drawn by osmosis from intracellular compartments and the extracellular fluid volume becomes expanded.
  • In patients with heart failure or pulmonary congestion, the volume overload exaggerates pulmonary edema. So mannitol is contraindicated in acute pulmonary edema



Goodman & Gilman's: The Pharmacological Basis of Therapeutics, 13th Edition, Page Number: 452

Mannitol

  • RAISED ICP AND BRAIN HERNIATION
  • Osmotic diuretics increase the osmolality of the extracellular fluid compartment and thereby shift water back into the extracellular compartment.

questions.stem: A patient was given Acetazolamide to correct metabolic alkalosis. Which of the following is incorrect about acetazolamide?

options.label: A
options.text: Competitively inhibits Carbonic anhydrase in PT

options.label: C
options.text: Should be avoided in sulfa drug allergy patients

questions.answerText: Competitively inhibits Carbonic anhydrase in PT
questions.solutionHtml:
Competitively inhibits Carbonic anhydrase in PT

Acetazolamide:


  • Noncompetitively but reversibly inhibits Carbonic anhydrase in Proximal tubule
  • Proximal tubular epithelial cells are richly endowed with the zinc metalloenzyme carbonic anhydrase, which is found in the luminal and basolateral membranes
  • Carbonic anhydrase inhibitors act on the luminal and basolateral enzymes
  • Carbonic anhydrase plays a key role in nahco3 reabsorption and acid secretion
  • Acetazolamide is a sulfonamide derivative and is to be avoided in sulfa drug allergy patients
  • Causes alkaline urine and Hypokalemia with metabolic acidosis

Mechanism of action

  • CA is also present in
  • Ciliary body of eye (Aquous humor formation)
  • Choroid plexus (CSF formation)

questions.stem: Which diuretic acts without requiring access to the renal tubular lumen?
questions.solutionHtml:
Aldosterone antagonists
  • Aldosterone antagonists act from the interstitial side of the tubular cell by combining with Aldosterone Receptor and inhibit the formation of AIPs
  • rest all other diuretics get secreted into the tubular lumen by their transporters and act from the luminal side of the nephron
  • Amiloride and triamterene block Renal Epithelial Na+ Channels in the luminal membrane of principal cells in late distal tubules and collecting ducts by binding to a site in the channel pore

questions.stem: The following drugs are used in the treatment of Liddle syndrome except:
questions.solutionHtml:
Spironolactone
  • Liddle syndrome (Pseudo aldosteronism): An autosomal dominant disorder
  • Mutations in the β or γ subunits lead to increased basal amiloride-sensitive sodium channel activity
  • Due to hyperactivity of the amiloride-sensitive sodium channel of the principal cell of the cortical collecting tubule
  • It includes early-onset severe hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis& low renin and aldosterone
  • Treatment of Liddle syndrome with amiloride or triamterene lowers blood pressure and corrects hypokalemia and acidosis
  • Spironolactone is not an effective treatment because the increased activity of the amiloride-sensitive Na+ channel is not mediated by aldosterone
  • It is the doc for Connis syndrome

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about Furosemide?
questions.solutionHtml:
Used in pulmonary edema
  • Furosemide is a rapidly acting diuretic (high ceiling diuretic)
  • Acts upon the thick ascending segment of the loop of Henle
  • It is used for acute hypercalcemia, HTN crisis CHF and acute pulmonary edema, because loop diuretics are so effective, they should be used with caution in patients who are likely to be particularly susceptible to volume contraction from excessive diuresis - an example would be the treatment of hypertension in the elderly with little or no edema

questions.stem: A patient with an infectious disease is being treated with an aminoglycoside antibiotic. Which of the following diuretics should be avoided, for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Furosemide
  • Both the loop diuretics and the aminoglycosides (tobramycin, streptomycin, gentamicin, others) are potentially ototoxic—capable of causing vestibular damage (e.g., balance problems) or cochlear damage (tinnitus or, in some cases, sensorineural hearing loss).
  • MOA
  • Synergistic ototoxic effects
  • The risk increases when these drugs are used in the presence of renal insufficiency. The increased salt content of the endolymph and direct toxic action on the hair cells in the internal ear appear to be causative

questions.stem: A 55-year-old patient with severe post-hepatitis cirrhosis is started on a diuretic for another condition. Two days later he is found in a comatose state. The drug most likely to cause coma in a patient with cirrhosis is:
questions.solutionHtml:
Acetazolamide
  • The carbonic anhydrase inhibitors cause metabolic acidosis and urinary alkalosis. Patients with severe impairment of liver function are unable to synthesize urea efficiently from ammonia and become dependent on renal excretion of ammonium ions to rid the body of nitrogenous wastes. However, in alkaline urine, the ammonium ion is rapidly converted to ammonia gas, which is very rapidly reabsorbed, with severe neurologic consequences (hepatic encephalopathy)Hence it is contraindicated in liver disease
  • Sites of Action
